AU.title: ABS Census — Special Short Form (SSF) / Household Form (HHF)
AU.description: Australia’s official homelessness estimates come from the Census. People not in a dwelling were usually interviewed with the paper Special Short Form (SSF) — a shortened Census Household Form (HHF) for people sleeping rough when field staff need to interview several people quickly. SSF was the primary method for NSW, Victoria, Tasmania, South Australia, and southern parts of WA and Queensland. NT and northern WA/Qld more often used the full HHF.
cues: Special Short Form (SSF) — shortened paper interview for people sleeping rough / not in a dwelling
Census Household Form (HHF) — full household form; also used in some rough-sleeping interviews (esp. NT, northern WA/Qld)
Where did you sleep on Census night? (SSF Q1) — street, landmark, suburb, postcode
Usual address can be recorded as none when someone has nowhere they usually live
AU.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? Australia’s official homelessness estimate comes from the Census Special Short Form (SSF) / Household Form (HHF). If Census field staff interviewed you with SSF or HHF on Census night, you were already counted officially.

AU:Darwin.title: ABS Census — Household Form (HHF) primary for NT rough sleeping
AU:Darwin.description: In the Northern Territory, people not in a dwelling were primarily enumerated by interview using the paper or online Census Household Form (HHF), not the Special Short Form.
cues: Census Household Form (HHF) — primary NT instrument for people not in a dwelling
Usual address / ‘none’ responses help classify temporary stays and rough sleeping
Supported accommodation and boarding-house lists also feed the homelessness estimate
National estimates still combine SSF + HHF + administrative lists across Australia
AU:Darwin.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? In Darwin / NT, people not in a dwelling were primarily enumerated with the Census Household Form (HHF), not the Special Short Form. If ABS interviewed you with HHF on Census night, you were already counted.

US.title: HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) Count — model survey tools
US.description: US Continuums of Care run an annual Point-in-Time count of sheltered and unsheltered homelessness on a single January night. HUD publishes optional model PIT survey instruments and a methodology guide; CoCs may adapt them but must collect HUD’s minimum required data elements.
cues: Where did you sleep last night? (shelter / outdoors / vehicle / other)
Household type — individual, adult-only, or family with children
Length of time homeless and whether homelessness has been long-term / repeated (chronic)
Veteran status, disability, and other HUD subpopulation questions on model interview forms
US.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? The US official figure comes from Continuum of Care Point-in-Time (PIT) counts. If outreach or shelter staff included you on the January PIT night, you were already counted in HUD’s national estimate.

CA.title: Everyone Counts — Survey on Homelessness (PiT Count)
CA.description: Canada’s nationally coordinated Point-in-Time Count (“Everyone Counts”) combines a one-night enumeration with a Survey on Homelessness (core screening + 15 standardized questions).
cues: Core screening: where are you staying tonight / did you sleep unsheltered or in shelter?
Demographics — age, gender, Indigenous identity, veteran status
Reasons for housing loss and how long you’ve been homeless
Income sources, health conditions, and service needs (core survey block)
CA.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? Canada’s Everyone Counts PiT uses a Survey on Homelessness. If you completed that survey (or were enumerated) on the local count night, you were already counted.

GB.title: England rough sleeping snapshot + Rough Sleeping Questionnaire
GB.description: England’s official autumn rough-sleeping snapshot is a single-night local-authority count or evidence-based estimate (DELTA return). Separately, MHCLG’s Rough Sleeping Questionnaire interviews people with recent rough-sleeping experience.
cues: Single ‘typical night’ between 1 Oct and 30 Nov (count or multi-agency estimate)
DELTA return: totals plus age, gender, nationality breakdowns
Rough Sleeping Questionnaire: homelessness history, support needs, public-service use
Statutory homelessness (H-CLIC) applications are a separate administrative series
GB.collectionFormLabel: England rough sleeping snapshot — technical report / DELTA methodology
GB.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? England’s official autumn rough-sleeping snapshot uses a local-authority count or evidence-based estimate (DELTA return), not this site’s anonymous form. If you were included in a street count or partner estimate in Oct–Nov, you were counted in the official snapshot.

UA.title: Ukraine — Ministry of Social Policy service statistics + Depaul methodology study
UA.description: Ukraine’s published official figure counts people who received services at homeless facilities (Ministry of Social Policy administrative data). Depaul Ukraine’s 2026 analytical report documents that methodology and estimates under-coverage; there is no public national street-interview form equivalent to ABS SSF or HUD PIT.
UA.urlLabel: Depaul Ukraine analytical report (EN PDF) — cites Ministry figure
cues: Ministry of Social Policy: people who received services at homeless facilities (admin count)
Depaul / Rating / Ptoukha Institute survey of people using homeless services in major cities
No public national rough-sleeping interview form equivalent to ABS SSF / HUD PIT
Depaul estimate range (57k–121k) is research, not the Ministry headline
UA.relatedLabel: Depaul Ukraine — Homelessness in Ukraine report page
UA.collectionFormLabel: Depaul Ukraine study (methodology + Ministry figure citation)
UA.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? Ukraine’s official Ministry figure counts people who received services at homeless facilities. If you are on those facility service records, you may already be in the Ministry total. There is no separate public national street-count form.

RU.title: Russia — Census homeless households + Form 4-Sobes (institutional)
RU.description: Russia does not publish an ETHOS-style national homelessness headcount. The census enumerates people in ‘homeless households’ where the census finds them. Separately, Rosstat Form 4-Sobes covers specialised social-assistance institutions for people without a fixed place of residence (admin institutional stats, not a public street questionnaire).
cues: Census: people in homeless households enumerated where the census finds them
Form 4-Sobes: institutions of social assistance for persons without fixed residence
Admin institutional statistics — not a public street-interview form
Evidence prevalence survey % must not be treated as a headcount
RU.relatedLabel: Form 4-Sobes (сводная) — Rosstat Order No. 196 instrument text
RU.alreadyCountedBlurb: Have I already been counted? If census enumerators recorded you in a homeless household, or if you were served by a Form 4-Sobes institution in the reference period, you may already appear in official census/admin stats. There is no public national rough-sleeping interview form like ABS SSF or HUD PIT.
